skill.name: aws-compliance-checker
skill.description: Automated AWS compliance checks for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2 using AWS CLI and boto3 examples.
skill.summary: Check AWS security controls against common compliance frameworks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives caused by markdown fences, AWS JMESPath backticks, documentation links, and 0.0.0.0/0 compliance checks. The confirmed risk is that runnable examples execute AWS CLI commands that enumerate account security posture and may expose sensitive cloud metadata. No prompt injection or unauthorized network exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Runnable AWS CLI and boto3 examples access account metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear read-only permission requirement and require user confirmation before running any account checks.

remediation.issue: Compliance outputs can expose sensitive AWS resource names and identity data.
remediation.suggestion: Redact user names, access key IDs, bucket names, VPC IDs, and account identifiers in shared reports.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences and shebangs create noisy static detections.
remediation.suggestion: Separate example scripts from explanatory text and label them as user-reviewed, read-only examples.

content.value_statement: Cloud teams need repeatable checks for AWS compliance gaps. This skill provides AWS CLI and boto3 examples for common audit controls.
actual_capabilities: Provides CIS AWS Foundations checks for IAM, logging, monitoring, and networking.
Identifies CloudTrail, AWS Config, S3 logging, and VPC flow log gaps.
Checks security groups for public SSH and RDP exposure.
Includes PCI-DSS and HIPAA example checks using boto3 and AWS CLI.
Generates a basic compliance report structure with pass and fail counts.
limitations: Requires AWS credentials with permission to read account configuration.
Provides example scripts, not a complete managed compliance scanner.
SOC 2 coverage is guidance level and not a full attestation workflow.
Outputs may include sensitive account metadata and resource names.

use_cases.title: Prepare for an AWS compliance review
use_cases.description: Run baseline checks before an internal or external audit.

use_cases.title: Find cloud security configuration gaps
use_cases.description: Review IAM, logging, encryption, and network exposure controls.

use_cases.title: Build repeatable audit scripts
use_cases.description: Adapt the sample commands into scheduled compliance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic CIS review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for common AWS account gaps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to guide a CIS AWS Foundations review for IAM, logging, and networking.

prompt_templates.title: Check PCI-DSS controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Review payment environment controls in AWS.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to identify AWS controls related to PCI-DSS network security, encryption, MFA, and logging.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a HIPAA evidence summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Collect evidence for healthcare security controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to summarize HIPAA-related AWS checks for access controls, audit controls, and encryption.

prompt_templates.title: Design continuous compliance reporting
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automation planning for recurring audits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to design a weekly AWS compliance workflow with read-only permissions, redacted reports, and exception tracking.

output_examples.input: Check my AWS account for CIS logging controls.
output_examples.output: A summary of CloudTrail, AWS Config, S3 access logging, and VPC flow log status with gaps highlighted.
A control-oriented report covering public network exposure, encryption status, MFA coverage, and CloudTrail presence.

output_examples.input: Help me plan continuous compliance monitoring.
output_examples.output: A weekly review plan with required permissions, checks to automate, report handling guidance, and exception documentation steps.

best_practices: Run checks with read-only AWS permissions whenever possible.
Redact account identifiers, user names, and resource names before sharing reports.
Validate results against the official framework version used by your audit.
anti_patterns: Do not run the examples with broad administrative credentials by default.
Do not treat sample checks as complete legal or certification evidence.
Do not publish raw compliance outputs that expose account structure.

faq.question: Does this skill change AWS resources?
faq.answer: The provided examples focus on read and describe operations. Review commands before running them in your environment.

faq.question: Which compliance frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: It includes examples for CIS AWS Foundations, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2 security controls.

faq.question: Can it replace a formal audit?
faq.answer: No. It helps find gaps and collect evidence, but auditors define final evidence requirements.

faq.question: What permissions are needed?
faq.answer: Use read-only permissions for IAM, CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs, AWS Config, EC2, RDS, and S3 checks.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: How should results be shared?
faq.answer: Share summarized findings and redact sensitive resource names, user names, and account details.
